case: P-1, a given for the whole of 2024: question 1's answer assumes it for January to March; question 2's answer contradicts it for July to December on a finding (the laptop reissued in July). The scopes never meet.
design: docs/adr/0011 'Premises': premise_inconsistent holds while standing answers assume and contradict the same premise revision over scopes that overlap; the ways out are all on the record and none forces either side: revise an answer, name the rebutting finding (the premise goes to the operator as a dispute, a request of kind premise), narrow a scope, or answer conditionally. Uncertainty alone holds nothing.

docs/adr/0011 'Premises': a citation's scope is its own narrowing (entities, times) inside the premise's, or the premise's at the revision it cites; two scopes overlap unless both name entities and share none, or both name times and no two ranges meet.
docs/adr/0011 'Premises': a contradiction that names a standing finding opens a premise dispute for the operator (one per premise revision), holding nothing.
docs/adr/0013 'The end of a run, under every stop policy': done finishes a run when every question has a disposition under the bar; a warning never holds.
